beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Merhaba, Liam. One Claude prompt. One virus, two oncoproteins, two tumor suppressors struck simultaneously — the HPV dual hit in three topology moves.

props.command: claude "Port the hpv-dual-hit plate into a Manim scene — PURPLE viral source diverges to two BLUE brake octagons with VERM X-marks, then converges to one GREEN output cluster."

beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — E6/p53 and E7/Rb diverge-then-converge topology
beats.narration_text: HPV does something unusual: one virus disables two independent tumor suppressors simultaneously. E6 tags p53 for destruction; E7 binds and inactivates Rb. This plate shows the diverge-then-converge topology of that double hit.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — PURPLE viral source labeled HPV; upper brake labeled p53/E6; lower brake labeled Rb/E7; convergence to unchecked division output

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — why simultaneous loss of two independent brakes causes rapid progression
beats.narration_text: The two brakes are independent. Losing one usually doesn't cause cancer — cells have backup pathways. But losing both simultaneously removes two layers of protection at once. That's why cervical cancer from HPV can progress so rapidly.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — stat card: HPV causes ~95% of cervical cancers, 570k cases/year; two-brake redundancy diagram; 'both must go' annotation

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the hpv-dual-hit plate from plates underscore gen dot py p-zero-eight into Manim. Topology is diverge-then-converge. One PURPLE seven-sided viral source at the left. Two BLUE octagon brake shapes — upper and lower — each with a VERM X-mark. One GREEN cluster of six circles at the right as the output. Animate: fade in the source, grow two diverging arrows from source to each brake, fade in both brakes simultaneously, create two VERM X-marks, grow two converging arrows from brakes to output cluster, fade in the output cluster.

props.command:
claude "Port the hpv-dual-hit plate from plates_gen.py p08() into Manim.
One PURPLE viral source diverges to two BLUE brake octagons with VERM X-marks,
then converges to one GREEN output cluster.
Animate: source, diverge, strike both brakes, converge to output."

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_HpvDualHit class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The source is a RegularPolygon with n=7 — seven sides, PURPLE. The brakes are RegularPolygon with n=8 — octagons, BLUE — placed at two y-positions offset above and below the centreline. The X-marks are two Line objects crossing at the brake centre, VERM, stroke-width eight. The topology is three movement phases: LaggedStart GrowArrow for the two diverging arrows together, FadeIn for both brakes simultaneously, then the X-marks appear with Flash. Finally GrowArrow for the converging pair and FadeIn for the GREEN output cluster.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_HpvDualHit
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
config.background_color = "#FFFFFF"
PURPLE="#CC79A7"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_HpvDualHit(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    sx,sy = -4.8, 0.0
    source = RegularPolygon(n=7,color=PURPLE,
      fill_color=PURPLE,fill_opacity=0.25,
      stroke_width=3.2).scale(0.72).move_to([sx,sy,0])
    brakes=[]; xmarks=[]
    for by in [1.5,-1.5]:
      br=RegularPolygon(n=8,color=BLUE,
        fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.20,
        stroke_width=3.0).scale(0.62).move_to([0.5,by,0])
      brakes.append(br)
      xm=VGroup(
        Line([0.5-0.3,by+0.3,0],[0.5+0.3,by-0.3,0],
          color=VERM,stroke_width=8),
        Line([0.5-0.3,by-0.3,0],[0.5+0.3,by+0.3,0],
          color=VERM,stroke_width=8))
      xmarks.append(xm)
    conv=[4.8,0.0]
    cluster=VGroup(*[Circle(0.22,color=GREEN,
      fill_color=GREEN,fill_opacity=0.65,stroke_width=1.8
      ).move_to([conv[0]+dx,conv[1]+dy,0])
      for dx,dy in [(-0.3,0.35),(0.3,0.35),(0.6,0),
                    (0.3,-0.35),(-0.3,-0.35),(-0.6,0)]])
    # choreography
    self.play(FadeIn(source))
    div_arrows=[Arrow([sx+0.78,sy,0],[0.5-0.72,by,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.8) for by in [1.5,-1.5]]
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in div_arrows],
      lag_ratio=0.2))
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(b) for b in brakes],
      lag_ratio=0.1))
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(x) for x in xmarks],
      lag_ratio=0.35))
    conv_arrows=[Arrow([0.5+0.72,by,0],[conv[0]-0.78,conv[1],0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.8) for by in [1.5,-1.5]]
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in conv_arrows],
      lag_ratio=0.2))
    self.play(FadeIn(cluster))
    self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_HpvDualHit — diverge, X-marks, converge to output
beats.narration_text: Run it. The PURPLE heptagon appears — that is HPV. Two arrows diverge from it toward the upper and lower brakes. Both BLUE octagons appear simultaneously — the brakes exist in parallel, not in sequence. Then the VERM X-marks appear on each, upper first, then lower. Two convergence arrows reach toward the output cluster, and the GREEN circles fade in. One source, two strikes, one outcome.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: stagger the two brake hits so they appear sequentially, not simultaneously. Upper brake and its X-mark appear with a Flash first — that is E6 hitting the p53 brake. Then the lower brake and its X-mark appear with a Flash — E7 hitting Rb. Only after both brakes are struck do the convergence arrows appear and the output cluster grows. Then Flash the output cluster in GREEN to show the consequence: unchecked division starting.

props.command:
claude "Revise: stagger the two brake hits so they appear sequentially, not
simultaneously. Upper brake X-mark appears with Flash first, then lower brake.
Output cluster only grows after BOTH brakes are struck. Then Flash the cluster."

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with staggered hits
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_HpvDualHitTiming — sequential brake strikes, output Flash
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. Upper brake appears with its X-mark and a vermillion Flash — E6 cuts p53. Pause. Then the lower brake appears with its X-mark and Flash — E7 cuts Rb. The stagger makes the two events distinct: they are separate oncoprotein actions, not a single simultaneous event. Only after both cuts do the convergence arrows grow. Then the output cluster appears and flashes green — unchecked division starting.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: One source, two separate strikes, one shared outcome. The staggered animation showed that both cuts must happen — not just one — before unchecked division starts.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: E6+E7 sequential dual hit; AND-gate logic (both required); 'strip this pattern for any multi-hit oncology plate'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third beat to the scene — after the output cluster flashes, show what happens if you restore one brake. Animate one of the X-marks fading out, the brake regaining full opacity, and one of the convergence arrows fading. The output cluster should dim to fifty percent opacity. Why run it? Because this is the logic of targeted therapy: you don't need to restore both brakes to have an effect. Showing one restoration partially suppressing the output cluster makes the therapeutic concept concrete — and it sets up the question of whether one brake is enough.

props.command:
claude "Add a 3rd beat: after the cluster flashes, animate one brake restoration.
One X-mark FadeOut, brake regains opacity 0.6, one convergence arrow FadeOut,
output cluster dims to fill_opacity 0.25 — partial suppression."
